title: Guilford County Confirms Seventeenth Case of Animal Rabies in 2026 - Guilford County (.gov)

analysis.time: Guilford County confirmed the seventeenth case of animal rabies in 2026 on November 4, 2026. The event date is November 4, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The case was confirmed in Guilford County, specifically in Browns Summit, North Carolina. The affected population includes residents and pets in the area.
analysis.event: A skunk on Deer Stand Court in Browns Summit tested positive for the rabies virus. This is the seventeenth confirmed case of animal rabies in 2026, reported by the Guilford County Health and Human Services Agency - Department of Public Health.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The risk is emphasized through public health guidance to avoid contact with wildlife and to supervise pets outdoors.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Guilford County Animal Services and the Health and Human Services Agency are providing information and guidance on rabies prevention. Residents are advised to contact Animal Control for more information and to report any stray animals.

analysis.brief_en: Guilford County, North Carolina, confirmed the seventeenth case of animal rabies in 2026 on November 4, 2026. The affected animal was a skunk found on Deer Stand Court in Browns Summit. The Guilford County Health and Human Services Agency - Department of Public Health reported the case, emphasizing the ongoing risk of rabies in the local wildlife population. Public health guidance includes avoiding contact with wildlife, supervising pets outdoors, and reporting stray animals to Animal Control. Residents are encouraged to contact Guilford County Animal Services at 336-641-2506 or Jorge Ortega at 336-641-3409 for more information on rabies prevention. The county also highlights the importance of vaccinating domestic pets and keeping food indoors to reduce the risk of rabies exposure.

analysis.time: The bill was sent for interim study by the full New Hampshire House in March and, with the 2026 session closed and the biennium winding down, was no longer eligible for passage.
analysis.location_and_population: While post-exposure treatment can prevent the disease from progressing if it is administered soon enough, once symptoms appear, the disease is considered incurable.
analysis.event: HB 1488 sought to broaden the allowed cases for rabies vaccine exemptions in New Hampshire under one condition: A pet has received a series of tests attempting to demonstrate that their immune system has responded to the vaccine.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: More than 150 dogs, most of them fluffy and weighing under 15 pounds, have passed through Arsenault's care over the years, she said.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Reaching a conclusion about what level of blood antibodies is enough to protect a dog requires testing on living animals.

analysis.brief_en: For household dogs, cats and ferrets, rabies is the only vaccine required by New Hampshire state law. (Photo by Sebastian Condrea/Getty Images) Last month, the House Environment and Agriculture Committee recommended reconsidering the contents of a sidelined bill from last session: House Bill 1488 , which sought to increase rabies vaccine exemptions for New Hampshire pets. The bill was sent for interim study by the full New Hampshire House in March and, with the 2026 session closed and the biennium winding down, was no longer eligible for passage. Instead, the committee voted, 10-1, to recommend the topic be addressed in future legislation. That move came as a surprise to some. "Truthfully, we didn't think it was going to go as far," said Dr. Jane Barlow Roy, who chairs the legislative committee of the New Hampshire Veterinary Medical Association.

analysis.location_and_population: Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Coonoor, Tamil Nadu, India.
analysis.event: A media delegation from Andaman and Nicobar Islands visited the Pasteur Institute of India in Coonoor to learn about rabies prevention and vaccine research. The visit was aimed at understanding the institute’s work in vaccine research, manufacturing, and disease prevention.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The delegation learned about the institute’s research programs, vaccine manufacturing processes, and the role it has played in producing vaccines for major infectious diseases. The experts advised maintaining strict precautions to keep the islands rabies-free, emphasizing the importance of immediate first aid and proper animal vaccination.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The institute plans to expand its capabilities by establishing new biosafety level facilities for the production of viral, bacterial, conjugate, and recombinant DNA vaccines. The visit provided valuable insights into vaccine research and public health preparedness.

analysis.brief_en: A media delegation from Andaman and Nicobar Islands visited the Pasteur Institute of India in Coonoor to learn about rabies prevention and vaccine research. Experts at the institute briefed the delegation on vaccine manufacturing processes and the importance of maintaining strict preventive measures to keep the islands rabies-free. They emphasized the need for immediate first aid and proper animal vaccination.
